question: A coordinate model contains two reference points $P(1,2,-1)$ and $Q(5,-2,3)$. A third point $R(7,-4,5)$ lies on the same directed line beyond $Q$. The students examine the component vectors connecting these points to determine the external division ratio. They then use the external section formula to verify that the recorded position of $R$ is consistent with the positions of $P$ and $Q$.(a) Write the position vectors of $P$, $Q$ and $R$.(b) Obtain the component forms of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{PR}$.(c) Determine the ratio in which $R$ divides $PQ$ externally.(d) Verify the position vector of $R$ using the external section formula.
explanation: (a)The position vectors are`\vec{p}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\vec{q}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}`and`\vec{r}=7\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}`(b)`\overrightarrow{PQ}=\vec{q}-\vec{p}\overrightarrow{PQ}=4\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}`Also,`\overrightarrow{PR}=\vec{r}-\vec{p}\overrightarrow{PR}=6\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+6\hat{k}`(c)Since`\overrightarrow{PR}=\frac{3}{2}\overrightarrow{PQ},`the point $Q$ lies between $P$ and $R$. Further,`\overrightarrow{RQ}=\vec{q}-\vec{r}=-2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}`Thus, $PR=6\sqrt{3}$ and $RQ=2\sqrt{3}$. Therefore,`PR:RQ=3:1`Hence, $R$ divides $PQ$ externally in the ratio $3:1$.(d)Using the external section formula,`\vec{r}=\frac{3\vec{q}-\vec{p}}{3-1}\vec{r}=\frac{3(5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})-(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})}{2}\vec{r}=\frac{14\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+10\hat{k}}{2}\vec{r}=7\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}`The given position vector of $R$ is verified.
